assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, active GLP-1(7-36) amide) led to a therapeutic class that has transformed diabetes and obesity care with outcome benefits; originality, clarity of mechanism and breadth of impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide actions, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide forms) form a plausible trio; Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's contribution is industrial drug design and long-acting analogue development, and a fair split between basic and drug-development credit is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is confirmed by large independent trials across several agents and indications, and the mechanism is stable; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around Mojsov and the Habener group (Habener is not in the credited names).
Whether the prize should reward physiology or the drug-development track.
Four credited names exceed the three-laureate limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing, later PERK and ATF6) and underlies understanding of proteostasis in secretory, metabolic, neurodegenerative and malignant disease; conceptually original and clean.
assessment.attribution: Mori (the UPR element and ER stress signalling in yeast and mammals) and Walter (Ire1 as the stress sensor, non-conventional mRNA splicing) are the evident pair; the credit is compact and well matched to a two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed by many independent groups for over two decades and is textbook material; recognition is mature, with disease-relevance still developing.
uncertainties: Others (for example Kaufman, Ron) may be argued to hold parts of the mammalian branches; I rely on recollection rather than verification of credit details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality; the discovery is both original and clinically decisive.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation, 4-1BB CAR-T in leukemia) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and first clinical gene-modified lymphocytes) form a reasonable trio, though Eshhar, Kuwana, and Finney/Seed lie outside the supplied credit and might be contested.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation exist; long-term follow-up is maturing, though solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity limits remain unresolved.
uncertainties: Early-concept credit (Eshhar and others) is outside the supplied names.
Compound discovery of concept, co-stimulation, and clinical translation may merit different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity, with broad transformative effect across systems neuroscience; its originality and methodological impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is crowded: Bamberg, Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin), Miesenböck (first genetically targeted photoactivation), Deisseroth and Boyden (neuronal channelrhodopsin application and tool development). My trio reflects concept, molecule and neuronal deployment, but any selection is contestable and six names are credited.
assessment.maturity: Widely and independently confirmed as a tool; therapeutic application (vision restoration) is only emerging, so the case rests on method and discovery impact.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited people is unresolved.
Tool-development prizes carry risk of being judged more as technology than as a discovery about physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids from Lgr5+ cells provide self-organizing mini-tissues for modelling physiology, development, infection and cancer, and for personalized medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers (Lgr5 stem cells, organoid culture lead) and Sato (first intestinal organoid culture) are a coherent pairing; the contribution of other organoid pioneers and of Wnt-pathway work is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Method is widely adopted and independently reproduced; clinical and translational utility is still emerging, so timing is early to moderate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Wnt and stem-cell field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis introduced anti-cytokine therapy and changed treatment of several inflammatory diseases; clear causal chain from mechanism to patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann (TNF dominance in the cytokine network of synovium) and Maini (clinical trials of infliximab) are a clean and complementary pair; antibody engineering by others lies outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Validated across many trials and indications over 25 years; mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for antibody generation (for example Vilcek, Le) is outside the supplied names.
Field may feel the work has been less recognized than its impact, but this does not alter the assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR signalling established a central regulator of growth and nutrient response with implications for cancer, metabolism, immunity and ageing; conceptually foundational.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and its role in growth control; Schreiber's work on rapamycin-FKBP12 binding and the mammalian target is also a decisive contribution. Sabatini's mTORC1 and nutrient-sensing work is credited but I omit him because of attribution complexity; I did not verify details.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed across organisms; clinical rapalog use is established, though much biology remains open.
uncertainties: Allocation across Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and Sabatini's contemporaries (Abraham, Sabers) is uncertain.
Complex multi-stage discovery with different parts possibly needing different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition by imatinib is the prototype of molecularly targeted cancer therapy and converted CML into a chronic, manageable disease.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis), Druker (clinical proof of principle) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a plausible trio; Janet Rowley and others on the underlying biology lie outside the supplied credit, and Lasker recognition covered several of these names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of outcome data and independent confirmation; recognition is arguably late.
uncertainties: Could be viewed as already well recognized by other prizes.
Chemistry credit (for example Zimmermann) is outside the supplied names.
